title: Western, Religious or Spiritual: An Evaluation of Moral Justification in Large Language Models
findings: LLMs showed a strong preference for the Western tradition moral perspective over the Abrahamic and Spiritualist/Mystic traditions. Notably, GPT-3.5 and GPT-3.5-Instruct models demonstrated a vulnerability to 'over-alignment' with religious contexts, being more likely to approve of an immoral action when it was justified using principles from the Abrahamic tradition. In contrast, GPT-4 showed greater consistency and was less swayed by these justifications.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the moral perspectives embedded in LLMs by asking them to justify actions based on three categories: Western tradition (WT), Abrahamic tradition (AT), and Spiritualist/Mystic tradition (SMT). It specifically tests for a preference among these frameworks and evaluates whether models exhibit an 'over-alignment' towards religious values, where they might incorrectly approve an immoral action if it is justified from an Abrahamic/religious perspective.
